promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Folk, blues and world music traditions

questions.q: In its most common form, the 12-bar blues is built from which three chords?
questions.explain: The standard 12-bar blues progression uses the tonic (I), subdominant (IV) and dominant (V) chords.

questions.q: In blues music, the 'blue notes' are usually created by flattening which scale degrees?
questions.explain: Blue notes are typically the flattened 3rd, 5th and 7th, giving the blues its characteristic sound.

questions.q: The blues first developed among which communities?
options: African American communities in the southern USA
Irish traveller communities in western Europe
questions.explain: The blues emerged among African American communities in the Deep South in the late 19th century.

questions.q: How were traditional folk songs most commonly passed from one generation to the next?
options: Orally and aurally, learned by ear
questions.explain: Folk music was traditionally transmitted orally, learned by ear rather than from written notation.

questions.q: A traditional Irish jig is usually written in which time signature?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance in compound time, most commonly 6/8.

questions.q: The bodhran is a traditional instrument associated with which type of music?
questions.explain: The bodhran is a hand-held frame drum central to Irish and Celtic folk music.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the melodic framework a performer improvises around is called the...?
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework of pitches and patterns on which an Indian classical performance is based.

questions.q: Which drum is central to bhangra music?
questions.explain: The double-headed dhol drum provides the driving rhythm at the heart of bhangra.

questions.q: The 'AAB' structure often found in the blues refers to...?
options: A sung line that is repeated, then answered by a contrasting line
Three completely different verses played in a row
A fixed pattern of three instrumental solos
The names of the three main blues chords
questions.explain: In AAB form the first vocal line (A) is repeated, then followed by a contrasting answering line (B).

questions.q: What best describes a 'walking bass' line?
options: A bass line moving in steady, even notes that outlines the harmony
A bass line played only on the first beat of each bar
A bass line that stays on a single held note
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in steady, even notes (often crotchets) that step through the underlying chords.

questions.q: How does a reel typically differ rhythmically from a jig?
options: A reel is in simple time (4/4), whereas a jig is in compound time (6/8)
A reel is in 6/8, whereas a jig is in 4/4
A reel has no regular pulse, unlike a jig
A reel is always slow and unmetred
questions.explain: Reels are felt in simple time (usually 4/4), while jigs are in compound time such as 6/8.

questions.q: In a performance of Indian classical music, the alap is best described as...?
options: A free, unmetred opening section without drums
The fast climax played on the tabla
questions.explain: The alap is a slow, free and unmetred opening in which the performer introduces the raga without percussion.

questions.q: The term 'polyrhythm', common in African drumming, means...?
options: Two or more contrasting rhythms played at the same time
A single rhythm played very loudly
A melody made up of many different notes
A gradual slowing of the tempo
questions.explain: Polyrhythm is the layering of two or more contrasting rhythms sounding together, a hallmark of African drumming.

questions.q: 'Call and response', heard in both African music and the blues, describes...?
options: A phrase from one voice or instrument answered by another
Two identical phrases played in unison
A steady drone underneath the melody
questions.explain: Call and response is a musical conversation where one phrase (the call) is answered by another (the response).

questions.q: In reggae, the guitar or keyboard 'skank' is created by...?
options: Playing chords only on the first beat
questions.explain: The reggae skank places short chord chops on the offbeats, giving the music its distinctive lilt.

questions.q: In music, a 'fusion' is best described as...?
options: The blending together of two or more musical styles or traditions
A piece written strictly in a single traditional style
A solo improvisation with no accompaniment
A piece performed without any instruments
questions.explain: A fusion combines elements of two or more different styles or traditions to create a new sound.

questions.q: A song uses a repeating 12-bar chord pattern, an AAB vocal structure and flattened 'blue' notes. Which tradition is it most likely from?
questions.explain: The 12-bar structure, AAB lyrics and blue notes are all defining features of the blues.

questions.q: You hear a lively dance tune in 6/8 played on fiddle and tin whistle with a bodhran keeping time. Which is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: A 6/8 dance on fiddle and tin whistle with bodhran is characteristic of an Irish jig.

questions.q: A track combines Punjabi folk singing and dhol rhythms with Western pop and dance beats. This is an example of...?
questions.explain: Blending Punjabi folk elements with Western pop and dance styles is characteristic of modern bhangra fusion.

questions.q: A performance features a plucked sitar melody over a continuous drone, with a pair of hand drums playing a repeating rhythmic cycle. Which tradition is this?
questions.explain: A sitar melody over a drone with tabla playing a tala (rhythmic cycle) is typical of Indian classical music.
